transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I'm just really struggling to even leave the house lately because of how awful my skin looks. I have these horrible, disgusting scars and acne all over my face, and it completely ruins my appearance. I feel like everyone is constantly staring at how ugly it is.
Can you tell me more about these scars and acne, how much time do you spend each day thinking about them or trying to hide them?

I easily spend three to four hours every single day just obsessing over every little mark and trying to cover them up. I have to layer on heavy makeup and wear hats to hide them because they look so hideous and obvious to me, even though my family claims they can't see anything.
How have these concerns about your skin affected your daily life, such as your relationships, work, or social activities, and have you noticed any significant distress or impairment as a result?

It has completely ruined my social life because I constantly cancel plans with my friends out of shame. I've also missed a lot of work lately because some days I just can't bring myself to let anyone see my face. The anxiety and distress are so overwhelming that I feel completely isolated.
Do you believe that your skin appearance is truly as flawed or abnormal as you perceive it to be, or do you have any moments where you question whether your concerns might be exaggerated?

I am absolutely certain that my skin is as deeply flawed and abnormal as I think it is. My concerns aren't exaggerated at all because I can clearly see these hideous marks every time I look in the mirror. Even if other people try to reassure me or say they can't see anything, to me, the scars are completely real and devastating.
Have you ever considered seeking a professional opinion from a dermatologist to assess the actual severity of your skin concerns, and would you be open to their feedback about your appearance?

I've actually gone to several dermatologists and specialists trying to get these scars and acne fixed. But it's incredibly frustrating because they always downplay my concerns and tell me my skin is fine, which just isn't true. I'm really hesitant to see anyone else because they never seem to take how severe it is seriously.

How do you think you would react if a dermatologist were to take high-quality photos of your skin and then show them to you, saying that from a medical perspective, your skin is within the normal range of appearance, would that change your perception of your skin at all?

Honestly, that wouldn't change how I feel at all, and I would just feel incredibly frustrated and misunderstood. When I look in the mirror, the scars and acne are so prominent and distressing that I'd assume the doctor was either missing something or just trying to be polite. I simply cannot ignore the hideous flaws that I clearly see with my own eyes.

The patient's refusal to accept external evaluations of their appearance and their insistence on the reality of their perceived flaws further support this diagnosis. No new information has been presented that would suggest considering alternative diagnoses from the allowed list, so the candidate list remains unchanged.
